research_question: Can context-aware, risk-aware, signal-adaptive navigation increase correctly confirmed medical messages per minute compared with conventional fixed-menu EEG communication?
disclaimer: SIMULATION ONLY. Decoder outcomes come from the real FBCCA code run on SYNTHETIC EEG; the patient is a perfect-intent simulated agent; profiles are synthetic. These are model estimates for comparing strategies, not empirical or clinical results.

mixes.matched: tasks drawn from the profile's request distribution (60% profile signals + 40% uniform)
mixes.uniform: tasks uniform over all 1,474 phrases (context gives no help)

conditions.label: D+: full NeuroSteno, confidence-gated step confirmation

metrics_definitions.cmpm: correctly confirmed messages per minute of task time (primary outcome)
metrics_definitions.selections_per_correct: accepted neural selections per correctly confirmed message
metrics_definitions.error_rate: wrong messages confirmed / all messages confirmed during tasks
metrics_definitions.idle_false_selections_per_min: selections accepted while the patient attended nothing
metrics_definitions.idle_false_sent_per_hour: messages sent while the patient attended nothing
metrics_definitions.urgent_mean_s: mean time to correctly confirm an urgent message (completed probes)

per_message.description: Single-message sessions for the demo scenario messages: same profile, message, signal level and seed for every condition. runs = replicates x message_runs.
per_message.final_sent_without_confirm_note: Simulator protocol counter (a message can only be sent after a decoded final YES); the live engine enforces and reports the same invariant in state.safety_invariants.

limitations: Synthetic EEG: SNR levels are simulator settings, not measurements from people; real SSVEP varies with the person, display, electrode contact and fatigue.
Perfect-intent patient model: no attention lapses, no changes of mind; only decoder errors occur.

The fixed-menu baselines A/B/C decode with conventional fixed-window forced choice and confirm only the final message; D uses dynamic stopping, abstention and per-step confirmation. Part of D's difference therefore comes from the decoder protocol, not only navigation; the per-condition rows separate the contributions.
A* is chosen in hindsight on the test results (oracle), which favours the baseline.
Tasks in the 'matched' mix come from the same request distribution the context router optimises for; the 'uniform' mix shows the cost when context does not match the patient's need.
Calibration estimates (used by C and D to pick n) come from 5 trials per target, as in the live protocol, and are optimistic in-sample; test outcomes are held out.
No real-EEG results are included. Real results must come from REAL-mode sessions and are reported separately.
